clue.text: Jerry perhaps recalled part in long-running play

indicators.note: something recalled is called back, so the word that follows is read from its end to its start

blocks.note: Jerry of Tom and Jerry is a cartoon mouse
taken as written, then turned round

explanation.surface: An actor once known as Jerry returns to a role in a show that has run for years.
explanation.walkthrough: THE MOUSETRAP, Agatha Christie's whodunnit, has run in London's West End since 1952, the longest run of any play.
explanation.definitionFit: Christie's thriller holds the world record for the longest continuous theatre run, so it is the long-running play par excellence.

clue.text: Film a cawing wingless bird

indicators.note: with its wings, the outer edges, clipped off, the phrase keeps only its central run of letters

blocks.note: the middle of the phrase, with the ends trimmed

explanation.surface: A director films a crow-like bird that has lost its wings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wingless' seems to describe the bird, but it means cut off the outer letters of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A macaw is a large, brightly coloured tropical parrot.

clue.text: Throws salt and processed nuts around

indicators.note: processed food has been worked over, so these letters are rearranged
around says one set of letters is placed so as to surround the other

blocks.note: the letters of nuts rearranged and split around the salt
the salt is a poetic name for the sea

explanation.surface: A cook tosses salt and roasted nuts into the mix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throws' as in a horse throwing its rider.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse that throws its rider unseats them, knocking them from the saddle.

clue.text: 7-1 is such a number

indicators.note: minus one takes away a single letter, here the opening one

blocks.note: the number written out as a word

explanation.surface: An arithmetic statement: seven take away one gives an even result.
explanation.walkthrough: The sum also works literally: seven minus one is six, which is even. '7' is a number, not a cross-reference to 7 Down.
explanation.definitionFit: An even number is one divisible by two, as six is.

clue.text: I race about and cause destruction

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word is wrapped round another

blocks.note: to race is to run
taken as written

explanation.surface: A reckless driver admits to speeding round and wrecking things.
explanation.definitionFit: To ruin is to wreck or destroy, so it means to cause destruction.

clue.text: Claimed USA plotted conflict

indicators.note: conflict suggests things clash and break apart, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: ten letters taken as written to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An allegation that America planned a war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conflict' reads as a noun, the war plotted; it is the instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To postulate is to put forward as true without proof, so postulated means asserted or claimed.

clue.text: Roughly put down cheap wine

blocks.note: first meaning: to set something down heavily and carelessly
second meaning: British slang for inexpensive, poor-quality wine

explanation.surface: Someone carelessly sets down a bottle of bargain wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Plonk is everyday British slang for cheap wine.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for dumping something down with a thud and a slang noun for inferior table wine.

clue.text: Free girl, one imprisoned by sicko

indicators.note: imprisoned by means held inside, so the first words go within the last

blocks.note: a perve (or perv) is slang for a pervert
a miss is a girl
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A newspaper headline about a girl freed after being held by a deviant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free' looks like a verb about releasing the girl; it is an adjective meaning liberal.
explanation.definitionFit: Permissive means allowing much freedom, especially in behaviour, so liberal or free.

clue.text: Stuff yourself on high tea after exercise

indicators.note: to exercise is to work something out, so the letters before it are worked into a fresh order

blocks.note: over means above, on high
the letters of tea rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice not to gorge at afternoon tea after a workout.
explanation.definitionFit: To overeat is to eat too much, which is to stuff oneself.

clue.text: Secret caress performed by typist

blocks.note: a key is the secret to something, as in the key to success
to stroke is to caress

explanation.surface: A furtive touch from someone in the typing pool.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes rather than names: what a typist performs, over and over, is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A keystroke is a single press of a key on a keyboard, the basic action a typist carries out.

clue.text: It drastically corrects my guise

indicators.note: a drastic change is a radical overhaul, so the letters that follow are thoroughly rearranged

blocks.note: fifteen letters taken as written to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A patient describes a procedure that radically remakes their appearance.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: read straight it describes the answer, while 'corrects my guise' is rearranged into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosmetic surgery is an operation to alter one's looks, which is exactly a drastic correction of one's appearance or guise.

clue.text: That which initially withstands hatred always triumphs

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the words that follow

blocks.note: the opening letters of the four words

explanation.surface: A moral maxim: whatever resists hatred will always win.
explanation.definitionFit: As a relative pronoun the word stands for the thing that, as in 'take what you need'.

clue.text: Basic right to university, a bit of money and books

definitions.note: a noun here, as in 'the basics': a fundamental element

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for right
U is the abbreviation for university
a dime is a US ten-cent coin
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A student lists essentials: a right to higher education, a little cash and some textbooks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Basic' looks like an adjective but is used as a noun, one of the basics.
explanation.definitionFit: A rudiment is a first principle or elementary point of a subject, which is one of the basics.

clue.text: Crazy family, cause of one's downfall?

blocks.note: bananas is slang for crazy
kin are relatives

explanation.surface: A mad family is blamed for someone's ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the joke: a downfall can be literal, a slip on the peel.
explanation.definitionFit: A banana skin is the classic slapstick cause of a fall, and figuratively any embarrassing blunder that trips someone up.

clue.text: Secret scam by crook with secret identity

indicators.note: keeping something secret means hiding it inside, so one piece is concealed within another

blocks.note: a con is a swindle
a fence is a criminal who handles stolen goods
ID is short for identity

explanation.surface: A fraudster with a hidden identity runs a covert swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Secret' appears twice: first as the definition, then as the signal that one piece is concealed in another. A fence is slang for a receiver of stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A confidence is something told privately in trust, a secret, as in 'share a confidence'.

clue.text: Dance supremo meets a star

blocks.note: a supremo is the person in charge
taken as written
a nova is a star that suddenly brightens

explanation.surface: At a dance, a big boss is introduced to a celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star' suggests a celebrity, but here it is the astronomical kind.
explanation.definitionFit: The bossa nova is a Brazilian style of music and the dance performed to it.

clue.text: Last drink? Cheers!

blocks.note: last in a list is at the bottom
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: A barman calls last orders and a drinker raises a toast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last drink?' reads as a closing-time question; it splits into two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are toasts said before drinking, the second urging people to tip the glass right up.

clue.text: Where badgers live, love and fight

blocks.note: a sett is a badger's burrow
love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A nature note: badgers' homes see both affection and scraps.
explanation.definitionFit: A set-to is a brief but fierce argument or scuffle, which is a fight.

clue.text: A drab, backward American city

indicators.note: backward tells us to read the preceding words from the end to the start

blocks.note: taken as written
drab is an old word for a slovenly woman, a slattern

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at a dull, behind-the-times US town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drab' looks like an adjective meaning dull, but it is an old noun for an untidy woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Tulsa is a city in Oklahoma, so it is an example of an American city.

clue.text: Rugby player's known in bar

blocks.note: a lock is a second-row forward in rugby
a secret that is out is known

explanation.surface: A rugby player is a familiar face in the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' suggests a pub; here it is a verb meaning shut out.
explanation.definitionFit: To lock out is to exclude people by keeping them from entering, which is to bar them.

clue.text: Reeve enthralled by imaginative serf's poetry

indicators.note: an imaginative version is freely reinvented, so these letters are reworked
to be enthralled is to be held captive, so one word is held inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written; a reeve was a medieval manor official
the letters of serf rearranged, split around the official

explanation.surface: A medieval official is captivated by a peasant's inventive poems.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Free verse is poetry written without regular metre or rhyme.

clue.text: I arrive abroad in coastal area

indicators.note: abroad suggests being scattered widely, so the letters are spread into a new order

blocks.note: seven letters taken as written to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker lands overseas at a seaside resort.
explanation.definitionFit: A riviera is a stretch of coast popular with holidaymakers, like the French Riviera.

clue.text: Source of fruit or vegetables

definitions.note: singular in the clue, plural answer: orchards in general are a source of fruit

blocks.note: taken as written
chard is a leafy vegetable

explanation.surface: A question of where produce comes from: fruit or veg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fruit or vegetables' reads as one phrase; the definition stops at 'fruit'.
explanation.definitionFit: Orchards are plantations of fruit trees, so they are where apples and pears are grown.

clue.text: About eggs, we hear

indicators.note: we hear points to a word that is spoken, not seen, so the spelling may differ

blocks.note: ova are eggs, and in a non-rhotic British accent the two words sound alike

explanation.surface: Someone passes on gossip concerning eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: Over and about both mean concerning, as in 'a row over money'.

clue.text: Girl is flipping eggs to make a sandwich

indicators.note: flipping something over turns it the other way, so the word is read backwards
a sandwich has a filling between two slices, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: roe is fish eggs
taken as written, then turned round

explanation.surface: A girl in a café kitchen tosses eggs for a sandwich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping eggs' looks like cooking; the flipping applies to 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosie is a girl's name, so it is an example of a girl.

clue.text: Hairstyle seen back in Forfar?

indicators.note: seen in means the letters sit visibly inside the following word
back tells us to read the run of letters from right to left

blocks.note: a run of four letters inside the word

explanation.surface: A question whether a certain hairdo is spotted in a Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: Forfar is a small town in Angus, Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: An Afro is a rounded, bushy hairstyle of tightly curled hair.

clue.text: Bolt is fast, for the most part!

indicators.note: for the most part means nearly all, so a final letter is dropped

blocks.note: fleet means swift

explanation.surface: An admiring remark about a sprinter, Usain Bolt, being quick nearly all the time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bolt' suggests the sprinter Usain Bolt; it is a verb meaning run off.
explanation.definitionFit: To bolt is to run away suddenly, which is to flee.

clue.text: For King cellists are, sadly, just minor diversions at Christmas

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters before it are put into a new order

blocks.note: fifteen letters taken as written to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Cellists playing for royalty at Christmas are lamented as mere side entertainment.
explanation.definitionFit: Stocking fillers are small, cheap presents put in a Christmas stocking, so minor seasonal amusements.

clue.text: Appoint a prominent Russian

blocks.note: first meaning: to install someone in a post
second meaning: Vladimir ..., the Russian leader

explanation.surface: Install a leading figure from Russia.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to place someone in office, and read as one word it is the surname of Russia's president.

clue.text: Former partner I judge to be free from blame

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner
I is the Roman numeral one
to rate is to assess or judge

explanation.surface: Someone decides their ex was not at fault after all.
explanation.definitionFit: To exonerate is to clear someone officially of guilt or wrongdoing.
